extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent applicants and their attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on making, supporting, and processing restriction requirements under 35 U.S.C. 121 and related PTO practice (identifying independent/distinct inventions, establishing search/examination burden, election of species, linking claims, telephone practice, and recordkeeping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions as claimed are independent if there is no disclosed relationship between the inventions, that is, they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more inventions are independent and there would be a serious search and/or examination burden on the examiner if restriction is not required, applicant should be required to restrict the claims presented to one of such independent inventions. Examples: (A) two different combinations not disclosed as capable of use together having different modes of operation, functions and effects (e.g., an article of apparel and a locomotive bearing); (B) process and apparatus where the apparatus cannot be used to practice the process (a specific molding process vs. a molding apparatus that cannot practice it). Form paragraphs 8.20.02 and 8.20.03 may be used to restrict between independent, unrelated inventions and between an unrelated product and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.20.02 — Unrelated Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when claims are presented to unrelated inventions; paragraph states that the inventions are unrelated if not disclosed as capable of use together and have different designs, modes of operation, and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Use only when inventions are unrelated (e.g., a necktie and a locomotive bearing). (2) Insert reasons in the bracket for concluding inventions are unrelated. (3) This form paragraph must be followed by form paragraph 8.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 8.20.03 — Unrelated Product and Process Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when inventions are directed to an unrelated product and process; product and process are unrelated if the product cannot be used in, or made by, the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Insert reasons for concluding inventions are unrelated. (2) This form paragraph must be followed by form paragraph 8.21. See MPEP § 802.01 and § 806.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability Report Practice Does Not Affect Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability report practice (MPEP § 705) has no effect upon, and does not modify in any way, the practice of restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentability reports are designed merely to facilitate handling of cases in which restriction cannot properly be required; they do not alter restriction practice or modify the requirements for restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for Insisting Upon Restriction — Two Aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Every requirement to restrict must include (A) the reasons why each invention as claimed is either independent or distinct; and (B) the reasons why there would be a serious search and/or examination burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both aspects must be addressed in the restriction requirement; mere conclusions are inadequate. See following MPEP sections for how to articulate each aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for Holding Independence or Distinctness — Statement Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The particular reasons relied on by the examiner for holding that the inventions as claimed are either independent or distinct should be concisely stated; a mere statement of conclusion is inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the factual/technical basis for the conclusion (e.g., for a combination vs subcombination, explain why the subcombination has utility by itself and why the combination does not require the particulars of the subcombination). Treat each relationship of claimed inventions similarly. Form paragraphs 8.01, 8.02, and 8.14–8.20.02 may be used as appropriate. See MPEP § 806.05–§ 806.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species — Independence/Distinctness and Restriction Permissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is no disclosure of a relationship between species, they are independent inventions; a restriction is permissible if there is a patentable difference between the species and a serious search/examination burden would result if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a relationship between species is disclosed, the disclosed relation must be discussed and reasons advanced showing the relation does not prevent restriction. Election of species should not be required between species considered clearly unpatentable (obvious) over each other; group species considered clearly unpatentable over each other. Election of species may be required prior to a search in some cases (e.g., species claims with no generic claims, or species plus generic/Markush claims). See MPEP §§ 803, 808.01(a), 803.02, 809.02(a), and 809.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing Burden — Requirements to Demonstrate Serious Search Burden
rubrics_metrics.description: When inventions are shown to be independent or distinct, the examiner must explain why there would be a serious search and/or examination burden if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To demonstrate serious search burden the examiner must show by appropriate explanation one of: (A) separate classification thereof (each invention is a separate subject and field of search); (B) a separate status in the art when classifiable together (evidence: patents showing separate status and separate field of search); or (C) a different field of search (necessity to search different classes/subclasses, electronic resources, or different search queries). Patents need not be cited to show separate classification or different fields of search. If classification and field of search are the same and no indication of separate future classification exists, no reasons exist for dividing inventions. To demonstrate serious examination burden separate from search, show that inventions are likely to raise serious examination issues (e.g., non-prior art issues under 35 U.S.C. 101, pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph, and/or 35 U.S.C. 112(a)) that are relevant to one invention but not the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Claims — When They Prevent Restriction and Rejoinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims (claims which, if allowable, would require rejoinder) may prevent restriction between otherwise divisible inventions; common linking claims are genus claims linking species and subcombination claims linking plural combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking claims and the inventions they link are usually all product claims or all process claims. If an application includes distinct inventions and linking claims, restriction can nevertheless be required. Linking claims must be examined with the elected invention and are considered part of it. When all claims directed to the elected invention are allowable, and any linking claim is allowable, the restriction requirement between the linked inventions must be withdrawn and nonelected claims depending from the allowable linking claim must be rejoined and fully examined (see 37 CFR 1.104 and MPEP § 821.04). If restriction is predicated on nonallowability of linking claims, applicant may retain claims to nonelected inventions; if nonelected claims were canceled under the restriction requirement they may be reinstated by amendment upon allowance of the linking claim. Where restriction requirement is withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 provisions no longer apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species Required — Identification and Reply Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction between species is appropriate, the examiner should send a restriction letter (or telephone requirement) identifying generic claims (or indicating none present), clearly identify each disclosed species (or exemplary ones), and require applicant to elect a single disclosed species under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify species preferably by figures or examples; if not, state mechanical means, material, or other distinguishing characteristics; if inconvenient to identify individual species, claims may be grouped by species. Provide reasons why species are independent or distinct. A complete reply must include a proper election and a listing of all claims readable on the election (including any claims subsequently added). Election may be with or without traverse; to preserve petition rights, election must be with traverse and traversal must be timely presented in the election reply (failure to timely traverse loses right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144). If only generic claims are presented, restriction cannot be required unless the generic claim encompasses such multiplicity of species that an unduly extensive search would be necessary. If applicant presents species claims after an Office action on only generic claims with no restriction, the Office may require election of a single species for examination. See form paragraph 8.01 and detailed examiner notes (bracket insertions and reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species When Only Generic Claim(s) Present
rubrics_metrics.description: When only generic claim(s) are presented but they are generic to multiple patentably distinct species, examiner should require election of a single disclosed species or grouping of patentably indistinct species for prosecution on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph template identifies claim numbers, lists species, states reasons, advises applicant of reply completeness (election and claim identification). Examiner notes instruct how to describe species and the applicable reasons for a serious search/examination burden (separate classification, separate status in art, different field of search, or relevant examination issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction Between Linked Inventions — When to Require and Form Paragraph 8.12
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application includes otherwise properly divisible inventions that are linked by a claim which, if allowable, would require rejoinder, the examiner should require restriction (written or telephoned). Use form paragraph 8.12 when linking claim is other than a genus claim linking species inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.12 identifies the linking claim(s), the inventions linked, and states that the restriction requirement as to the linked inventions is subject to nonallowance of the linking claim(s). Upon indication of allowability of linking claim(s), restriction is withdrawn and claims depending from or requiring all limitations of the allowable linking claim will be rejoined and fully examined per 37 CFR 1.104. Applicant should be advised about possible provisional statutory/nonstatutory double patenting rejections in divisional applications when divisional claims are anticipated by or include all limitations of the allowable linking claim. Examiner notes: include bracket insertions and references to related form paragraphs (8.45, 8.46, 8.47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Restriction Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner determines a restriction requirement should be made, the examiner should draft the requirement and telephone the attorney/agent to request an oral election, with or without traverse, and arrange a second call generally within 3 working days to allow consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If attorney/agent objects or fails to respond, mail a restriction requirement referencing the unsuccessful call. When an oral election is made, incorporate into the next Office action a formal restriction requirement including date of election, attorney/agent name, and a complete telephone interview record, followed by a complete action on the elected invention (including linking/generic claims if present). No telephone communication is needed if the requirement is complex, applicant is pro se, or examiner knows an election will not be made by telephone. Use form paragraphs 8.23, 8.23.01, 8.23.03 for telephonic election/attempts/no-telephone-permitted. Telephone practice is not permitted where no valid power of attorney is of record (use form 8.23.03). If telephonic election causes belief that C* classification picture is incorrect, examiner should submit a C* classification challenge and document the internal “Telephonic Restriction and Election Summary” (not mailed) with required details. Telephone restriction practice is limited to examiners with negotiation authority or with prior supervisory approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Making Requirement — Timing and Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.142(a) indicates a restriction requirement will normally be made before any action upon the merits; however, it may be made at any time before final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should make a proper requirement as early as possible in prosecution, ideally in the first action. Before requiring restriction of claims previously examined on the merits, consider whether there will be a serious search and/or examination burden. A second requirement may be made later if it becomes proper even though prior requirement was complied with. Where a requirement was made and later withdrawn as improper, if restriction becomes proper later it may again be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on the Merits and Finality Related to Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: When a restriction requirement is made without action on the merits, a 2-month shortened statutory period is set for reply; the Office action making the restriction requirement final ordinarily includes an action on the merits of elected claims. If a telephone restriction leads to an oral election, the written record will be accompanied by a complete action on the merits of elected claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If election is made with traverse and the examiner finds the elected claims allowable, it is proper to make the restriction requirement final after considering traversal reasons. See MPEP § 706.07(a) re: final actions. If elected invention is found allowable and no nonelected invention is eligible for rejoinder, attach restriction to Notice of Allowability form PTOL-37, include cancellation of nonelected claims, and a statement that prosecution is closed. If restriction is predicated on nonallowability of linking/generic linking claims, applicant can retain nonelected claims; canceled nonelected claims may be reinstated by amendment upon allowance of linking claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate Exactly How Application Is To Be Restricted — Recordkeeping/Clarity Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide a clear and detailed record of the restriction requirement to provide a clear demarcation between restricted inventions so it can be determined whether claims in a divisional are consonant with the restriction requirement and therefore subject to the prohibition against double patenting rejections under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear demarcation supports later determinations of consonance and double patenting. Use appropriate form paragraphs and fully document species/groups, reasons for restriction, claims corresponding to each group, election details, and any classification challenges. See MPEP § 804.01 and related case law (e.g., Geneva Pharms., Inc. v. GlaxoSmithKline PLC).
